neighbours.label: High-energy astrophysics of compact objects: accretion onto black holes, neutron stars and white dwarfs, accretion disks, relativistic jets and cataclysmic variables; quiet on 'accretion' in geology, on spaceflight and on everyday words starting with 'acc'.
fire: Matter falling toward the neutron star heats up in a thin accretion disk and glows in X-rays.
The quasar's relativistic jets extend far beyond its host galaxy.
In a cataclysmic binary, the white dwarf pulls gas off its companion star.
As the accretion rate rises, the disk around the black hole becomes brighter.
Tidal forces tore the star apart, and its debris spiraled into the black hole.
Blazars are active galaxies whose jets point almost directly at Earth.
Gas stripped from the giant star forms a swirling disk around the compact companion.
X-ray binaries flicker as clumps of gas fall onto the neutron star.
quiet: Slow accretion of silt at the river mouth built a delta over centuries.
The probe launched on a heavy rocket and reached orbit after nine minutes.
The astronauts repaired a solar panel during a long spacewalk.
The telescope photographed craters on the Moon from the observatory roof.
The accountant checked every receipt before closing the books.
Trains accelerate slowly when they leave the mountain station.
Coral reefs grow by the accretion of calcium carbonate from tiny animals.
She baked a pie and left it to cool on the windowsill.

predictions: median fire ~0.45 (probes: accretion disk 0.46, white dwarf accretion 0.32, cataclysmic variables 0.75, jets 0.46); near misses < 0.03 (sediment accretion 0.018, rocket 0.011, accountant 0.007, accelerate 0.017).
notes: Meaning without the word: jets and cataclysmic variables fired without 'accretion'. Word without the meaning: sediment accretion stayed at 0.018.
